newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq pardons Kurdish deserters - news agency.
newsitem.headline: Iraq pardons Kurdish deserters - news agency.

text.p: Iraq's all-powerful Revolutionary Command Council (RCC) has offered an amnesty to Iraqi Kurdish army deserters who "return to the national fold," the official Iraqi News Agency INA reported on Thursday.

"The Revolutionary Command Council, the highest legislative authority in Iraq, decided to stop all legal measures against Iraqi Kurdish militarymen...living in the autonomous region (of Kurdistan) who return to the national fold," INA said.

The Kurdish north has been under the control of the Kurds since after the 1991 Gulf War following Iraq's invasion of Kuwait. The area is patrolled by U.S. and British warplanes to protect it from Iraqi forces.

The Iraqi government has since then gained some power in the region when the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) leader Massoud Barzani last August asked Baghdad to send troops to help him fight against his rivals the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) led by Jalal Talabani.
The move prompted the United States to launch two waves of missile strikes against military targets in southern Iraq.
INA said the amnesty covers all Kurdish servicemen except "those who committed murder, rape and plundered state property."
Last September, Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein, who chairs the RCC, issued a broad amnesty to Iraqi Kurds and lifted Baghdad's embargo on their self-ruled areas.
